1. Engagement Scope

ACPWB was engaged by Perihelion Satellite Solutions to conduct an independent compliance assessment of workforce compensation programs following an internal audit exception identified in Q3 1999. This report summarizes findings, risk ratings, and corrective action requirements for 91 employee records reviewed across 19 locations.

2. Methodology

The assessment of §409A compliance included a detailed review of plan documents for documentary compliance and transactional testing of 91 deferral elections and distributions for operational compliance.

4. Detailed Findings
CIM-7967-001LOWIN PROGRESS
Observation

ADA interactive process not documented for 91 accommodation requests reviewed during the period

Corrective Action Required

Establish a formal process for reviewing and responding to all accommodation requests under the ADA and PWFA, including standardized forms for documenting the interactive process.

Management Response

While we accept the factual basis of the finding, we have performed a risk assessment and formally accepted the residual risk. This decision has been documented and approved by the Chief Risk Officer. No further corrective action is planned at this time.

Owner: Senior Analyst, Data Science • Due: 1999-05-28
CIM-8100-002INFORMATIONALREMEDIATED
Observation

10b5-1 trading plan for 91 executives lacks required cooling-off period under amended rules

Corrective Action Required

Develop and distribute a manager and HR guide on USERRA reemployment rights and obligations. Conduct mandatory training for all hiring managers and HR business partners.

Management Response

The finding is valid. The required report has been developed and is now generated and distributed automatically on a weekly basis. See attached sample report as evidence.

Owner: Vice President of Research • Due: 1999-05-28
CIM-3583-003HIGHIN PROGRESS
Observation

USERRA reemployment rights not properly communicated to 91 employees on military leave

Corrective Action Required

The Legal and HR departments will jointly develop a RIF playbook that includes a detailed WARN Act compliance checklist and a multi-level review process.

Management Response

We concur with the finding. The process has been redesigned, and user acceptance testing is scheduled for the week of 1999-04-12. Full implementation will follow immediately after successful testing.

Owner: Director of Information Security • Due: 1999-07-28
CIM-4157-004INFORMATIONALDEFERRED
Observation

OSHA 300A summary not certified by a company executive for 19 establishments

Corrective Action Required

The vendor onboarding process will be updated to include a mandatory, risk-based anti-corruption due diligence step for all international third-party intermediaries.

Management Response

Management agrees with the finding. The issue has been added to the agenda for the next quarterly business review with the responsible process owners to ensure accountability.

Owner: Director of Global Expansion • Due: 1999-05-28
CIM-6997-005HIGHMONITORING
Observation

Proxy statement CD&A omits required discussion of Massachusetts Wage Act; San Francisco Paid Parental Leave Ordinance; Newborns' and Mothers' Health Protection Act; OFCCP Executive Order 11246 (affirmative action obligations) performance metrics

Corrective Action Required

The Tax department shall perform a look-back analysis to identify all non-deductible compensation under §162(m) for the past three fiscal years and file amended returns if necessary.

Management Response

The finding is accepted. The required training has been developed and assigned to all 91 affected employees with a mandatory completion date of 1999-04-12. Completion rates will be tracked and reported to the compliance department.

Owner: Chief Operating Officer • Due: 1999-05-28
